description: Baseline: untouched production source. Hermes median-of-3 process runs; interleaved candidate/original samples remove order bias.

E1: per-call Map memoization of lowercase/needsMetadata/chain verdicts. Parity OK but SLOWER: primary 2.0 vs 1.667 baseline, small 0.202 vs 0.164, large 5.9 vs 5.6. At ~30% cross-account duplication (850 occ / 595 uniques on main), Map get/set per occurrence + 600 warm inserts for knownMetadataIds cost more than recomputing 1 toLowerCase + 2 object lookups.

asi.lesson: memo maps lose at 30% dup on Hermes; recompute is cheap; only consider memo for the expensive staking predicate if dup rate is high

description: E2: single toLowerCase per occurrence (lowerAssetId reuse), needsMetadata-before-chainFilter swap, Object.keys over entries, hoisted responseMetadata, loop-built knownMetadataIds. Checks pass (20 tests). Primary FLAT: 1.7/1.7/1.733 vs 1.7 baseline (swap added metadata+staking work for chain-filtered-out assets, cancelling the alloc savings on main where only 3/5 chains in scope). Large input consistently ~12% better: 4.833-4.933 vs 5.5-5.583 (all 5 chains in scope there, so the swap cost nothing; wins came from alloc trims + lowerId dedupe). Foundation for E3.

asi.lesson: large-input win shows alloc/lowercase trims are real; main flat because ordering swap hurt chain-filtered shapes; staking check hypothesized as dominant per-occurrence cost (~60% of occurrences reach isStakingContractAssetId: 2 regex + 2 allocs each)

description: E3: staking prefix precheck (sound: a staking ID must start with '${chainId}/erc20:' for a getSupportedStakingChainIds() chain since the CAIP regex anchors chainId+namespace at the string start) + single toLowerCase per occurrence + needsMetadata-first ordering + E2 alloc trims. Primary 1.083/1.083/1.1 vs 1.7 baseline (-36%); small 0.104 vs 0.166 (-37%); large 2.95 vs 5.5 (-46%). 20/20 tests + no type errors. Staking predicate (2 regex + 2 allocs) was the dominant per-occurrence cost.

E4: closure-free prefix loop (for..of + startsWith instead of .some closure per needsMetadata call). Flat: 1.083/1.067 vs 1.083 best, small 0.102-0.108 vs 0.104. Closure alloc too cheap to measure beyond noise on Hermes. Fold into next experiment if it wins.

E5: skip hasMetadataUsedByClients call when the metadata entry is undefined (+ E4 closure-free prefix loop). Flat/noisy: 1.05/1.1/1.133 vs 1.083 best; small 0.102-0.11; large 2.85-3.15. Calling the helper with undefined was already cheap on Hermes; stateEntry is defined for ~70% of assets so most calls remain. Call-overhead elimination is not measurable at this input scale.

asi.lesson: hermes small-call overhead negligible here; do not chase

description: E6: chainFilter prefix precheck before parseCaipAssetType in inRequestChains (sound: in-scope chainId must appear as `${chainId}/` prefix; anchored regex, no '/' in chainId charset). Primary 1.033/1.05/1.033 vs 1.083 (E3) = -4.6% beyond noise, -39% vs 1.7 original; small 0.098-0.1 vs 0.104; large_partial (new 8-acct x 3-chain sweep point) 2.85 vs 4.8 original (-41%); full-scope large 3.1-3.25: +5-8% vs E3 but still -44% vs 5.65 original - no regression vs production anywhere. 20/20 tests, no type errors.

asi.note: added large_partial sweep point per keep-gate rule (re-test with more data points); E6 beats original on every input; tradeoff vs E3 only on full-chain-scope shapes where every asset is in scope so the precheck is pure overhead

description: E7: re-swap state-loop order to chainFilter-precheck-first (skip needsMetadata for out-of-scope assets). WORSE: primary 1.067/1.067/1.067 vs 1.033 best (+3.3%), large 3.35-3.5 vs 3.1-3.25. Cost model wrong: the 3-prefix startsWith loop is pricier than needsMetadata's early exits; needsMetadata-first lets complete-metadata/hidden/staking assets skip the prefix loop entirely. E6's order is optimal.

asi.lesson: with both predicates cheap, keep expensive-last: needsMetadata-first pays precheck only for needing assets; chain-first pays precheck for all
